**Indore** ([/ɪ n ˈ d ɔːr/](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:IPA/English "Help:IPA/English")[](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/transcoded/6/64/Indore.ogg/Indore.ogg.mp3 "Play audio")[ⓘ](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Indore.ogg "File:Indore.ogg"); [ISO](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_15919 "ISO 15919"): _Indaura_, Hindi:[[ɪn̪d̪ɔːr]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:IPA/Hindi_and_Urdu "Help:IPA/Hindi and Urdu")) is the largest city of the [Indian state](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_state_and_union_territory_capitals_in_India "List of state and union territory capitals in India") of [Madhya Pradesh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Madhya_Pradesh "Madhya Pradesh") where it serves as the [capital](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_state_and_union_territory_capitals_in_India "List of state and union territory capitals in India") and the administrative headquarters of the eponymous [district](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore_district "Indore district") and [division](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore_division "Indore division"). Modern-day Indore was established on the banks of the [Kanh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kanh_River "Kanh River") and [Saraswati](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saraswati_River_(Madhya_Pradesh) "Saraswati River (Madhya Pradesh)") rivers and traces its roots to its 16th-century founding as a trading hub between the [Deccan Plateau](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deccan_Plateau "Deccan Plateau") and [Delhi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Delhi "Delhi").[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-11)[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-12) Following the conquest of [Malwa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malwa "Malwa") by [Peshwa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peshwa "Peshwa")[Baji Rao I](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Baji_Rao_I "Baji Rao I"), the city came under the control of the [Maratha Empire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maratha_Confederacy "Maratha Confederacy") until its annexation by the [British East India Company](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_East_India_Company "British East India Company").[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-13)[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-14) Prior to [Indian independence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_independence_movement "Indian independence movement"), [the Kingdom of Indore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore_State "Indore State") was a nineteen [Gun Salute](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Salute_state "Salute state")[Princely State](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Princely_State "Princely State") of the [British Raj](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_Raj "British Raj") with the [Holkars](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/House_of_Holkar "House of Holkar") as rulers.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-15)

With an estimated population of 5.6 million in 2025 distributed over nearly 10 thousand square kilometres, the metropolitan region encompassing Indore, [Ujjain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ujjain "Ujjain"), [Dewas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dewas "Dewas"), [Pithampur](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pithampur "Pithampur") and [Nagda](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nagda "Nagda") serves as the financial capital of Madhya Pradesh. One of India's main industrial hubs, the metropolitan region is a major center for pharmaceutical and automotive manufacturing with, notably, [Asia’s longest test track](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NATRAX "NATRAX").[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-16)[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-17)[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-18)[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-19)[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-:6-20)

The largest education hub in central India, it is home to an [Indian Institute of Technology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_Institute_of_Technology_Indore "Indian Institute of Technology Indore") and an [Indian Institute of Management](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_Institute_of_Management_Indore "Indian Institute of Management Indore") and is one of the cities selected under the [central government's](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Government_of_India "Government of India") flagship [Smart Cities Mission](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smart_Cities_Mission "Smart Cities Mission") and [Swachh Survekshan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Swachh_Survekshan "Swachh Survekshan") programmes.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-21)[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-22)[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-23)[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-24)

Consistently ranked as India's [cleanest city](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_cleanest_cities_in_India "List of cleanest cities in India"), Indore is regularly commended for its clean air and proper waste management.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-25)[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-26)[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-27)[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-28)[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-29)[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-30)

## Etymology

[Gupta](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gupta_Empire "Gupta Empire") inscriptions name Indore as "Indrapura".[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-auto1-31) It is believed that the city is named after its Indreshwar Mahadev Temple, where [Shiva](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shiva "Shiva") is the presiding deity.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-32)[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-33) It is believed that [Indra](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indra "Indra") himself did _[Tapasya](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tapas\_(Indian\_religions) "Tapas (Indian religions)")_ (meditation) in this place and led sage Swami Indrapuri to establish the temple. Later, [Tukoji Rao Holkar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tukoji_Rao_Holkar "Tukoji Rao Holkar") who belonged to the Holkar clan of the Marathas and was the feudatory of Indore, renovated the temple.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-34) The older name of Indore is believed to be **Indur**, as referenced in historical records.[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-35) In 2017, a proposal was brought forward by the Indore Municipal Corporation to rename the city as "Indur".[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-36)[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-37)

## History

### Gupta Empire (Gupta era)

[Gupta Empire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gupta_Empire "Gupta Empire") inscription mentions Indore as city/town of Indrapura in Gupta Indore Copper plate inscription dated 146 Gupta era or 465 CE.[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-38) These are also some of the earliest mentions of Indore where the city is mentioned as 'Indrapura'.[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-39) Indrapura (modern day Indore) was then known for its sun temple, where in 464–65 CE, Gupta king [Skandagupta](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Skandagupta "Skandagupta") had made an endowment for the permanent maintenance of the city's sun temple. The temple was constructed by two merchants of the city – Achalavarman and Bhṛikuṇṭhasiṁha.[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-auto1-31)[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-40)

### Holkar era (Maratha Empire)

Main article: [Holkar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Holkar "Holkar")

During the [Mughal era](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mughal_Empire "Mughal Empire"), the area under the modern Indore district was equally divided between the administrations (_[sarkar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sarkar\_(administrative\_division) "Sarkar (administrative division)")_ s) of [Ujjain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ujjain "Ujjain") and [Mandu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mandu,_Madhya_Pradesh "Mandu, Madhya Pradesh"). Kampel was the headquarters of a _mahal_ (administrative unit) under the Ujjain _sarkar_ of [Malwa Subah](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malwa_Subah "Malwa Subah") (province). The area of the modern Indore city was included in the [Kampel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kampel,_Indore "Kampel, Indore")[pargana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pargana "Pargana") (administrative unit).[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-gazetteer_1971-41)

In 1715, the [Marathas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maratha_Empire "Maratha Empire") invaded this region (Mughal territory) and demanded [chauth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chauth "Chauth") (tax) from the Mughal _Amil_ (administrator) of Kampel. The Amil fled to [Ujjain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ujjain "Ujjain"), and the local [zamindars](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zamindar "Zamindar") agreed to pay Chauth to the Marathas. The chief zamindar, [Nandlal Chaudhary](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rao_Nandlal_Chaudhary "Rao Nandlal Chaudhary") (later known as Nandlal Mandloi), paid a chauth of around Rs. 25,000 to the Marathas. [Jai Singh II](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jai_Singh_II "Jai Singh II"), the Mughal Governor of Malwa, reached Kampel on 8 May 1715, and defeated the Marathas in a battle near the village. The Marathas came back in early 1716, and raided Kampel in 1717. In March 1718, the Marathas, led by [Santaji Bhonsale](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bhonsle_(clan) "Bhonsle (clan)"), invaded Malwa again, but were unsuccessful this time.

By 1720, the headquarters of the local pargana were transferred from Kampel to Indore, due to the increasing commercial activity in the city. In 1724, the Marathas under the new [Peshwa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peshwa "Peshwa")[Baji Rao I](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Baji_Rao_I "Baji Rao I"), launched a fresh attack on the Mughals in Malwa. Baji Rao I himself led the campaign, accompanied by his lieutenants [Udaji Rao Pawar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dhar_State "Dhar State"), [Malhar Rao Holkar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malhar_Rao_Holkar "Malhar Rao Holkar") and [Ranoji Scindia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ranoji_Scindia "Ranoji Scindia"). The Mughal [Nizam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Qamar-ud-din_Khan,_Asaf_Jah_I "Qamar-ud-din Khan, Asaf Jah I") met the [Peshwa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peshwa "Peshwa") at [Nalchha](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nalchha "Nalchha") on 18 May 1724, and acceded to his demand of collecting chauth from the area. The Peshwa returned to the [Deccan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deccan "Deccan"), but left [Malhar Rao Holkar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malhar_Rao_Holkar "Malhar Rao Holkar") at Indore to oversee the chauth collection.

The Marathas maintained friendly relations with Nandlal Chaudhary, who held influence over the local [Sardars](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sardar "Sardar") (chiefs). In 1728, they defeated the Mughals decisively in the battle of [Amjhera](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battles_involving_the_Maratha_Empire "Battles involving the Maratha Empire"), and consolidated their authority in the area over the next few years. On 3 October 1730, [Malhar Rao Holkar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malhar_Rao_Holkar "Malhar Rao Holkar") was appointed as the Maratha chief of [Malwa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malwa "Malwa"). The local zamindars, who had the title of [Chaudhari](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chowdhury "Chowdhury"), came to be known as _Mandloi_ s (after [mandal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tehsil "Tehsil"), an administrative unit) during the [Maratha reign](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maratha_Empire "Maratha Empire"). The [Holkar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/House_of_Holkar "House of Holkar") dynasty of the Marathas, which controlled the region, conferred the title of _Rao_ upon the local zamindar family.[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-42) After Nandlal died, his son Tejkarana was accepted as the _Mandloi_ of Kampel by the [Peshwa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peshwa "Peshwa")[Baji Rao I](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Baji_Rao_I "Baji Rao I"). The pargana was formally granted to [Malhar Rao Holkar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malhar_Rao_Holkar "Malhar Rao Holkar") by merging 28 and one-half Pargana by the Peshwa in 1733. The pargana headquarters were transferred back to Kampel during his reign. After his death, his daughter-in-law [Ahilyabai Holkar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ahilyabai_Holkar "Ahilyabai Holkar") moved the headquarters to Indore in 1766. The [tehsil](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tehsil "Tehsil") of Kampel was converted into Indore tehsil by a change in the name.[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-gazetteer_1971-41) Ahilyabai Holkar moved the state's capital to [Maheshwar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maheshwar "Maheshwar") in 1767, but Indore remained an important commercial and military centre.

### Princely State (Indore/Holkar State)

Main article: [Indore State](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore_State "Indore State")

See also: [Dewas Junior](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dewas_Junior "Dewas Junior"), [Dewas Senior](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dewas_Senior "Dewas Senior"), [Dhar State](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dhar_State "Dhar State"), and [Gwalior State](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gwalior_State "Gwalior State")

[![Image 22](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/25/Ahilya_Bai_Holkar_2025_stamp_of_India.jpg/250px-Ahilya_Bai_Holkar_2025_stamp_of_India.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Ahilya_Bai_Holkar_2025_stamp_of_India.jpg)

[Ahilyabai Holkar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ahilyabai_Holkar "Ahilyabai Holkar") on a 2025 stamp of India

[Ahalyabai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ahilyabai_Holkar "Ahilyabai Holkar") Holkar is fondly remembered as a noble, saintly and courageous woman. She ruled the kingdom of Indore (which was then part of the wider [Maratha Empire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maratha_Empire "Maratha Empire")) for several decades. Her rule is remembered as a golden age in Indore's history. From an agricultural background herself, she married Khande Rao, prince of Indore. Thereafter, she resided in the Royal Palace. Later, she was trained in statecraft and accompanied the army to war on many occasions. At that time the [Maratha Empire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maratha_Empire "Maratha Empire") (which was founded by [Chhatrapati Shivaji Raje Bhonsale](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shivaji "Shivaji")) was at the apex of its power. There were frequent battles and skirmishes, both against foreigners as well as internal feuds. In one such battle in 1754, [Ahalyabai's](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ahilyabai_Holkar "Ahilyabai Holkar") husband was killed. Her aged father-in-law ([Malhar Rao](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malhar_Rao_Holkar "Malhar Rao Holkar")) was shattered at the death of his son. He summoned Ahalyabai, who he loved deeply, and said: "You are now my son. I wish that you look after my kingdom".[Malhar Rao Holkar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malhar_Rao_Holkar "Malhar Rao Holkar") died in 1766, 12 years after the death of his son Khande Rao. Malhar Rao's grandson and Khande Rao's only son [Male Rao Holkar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Male_Rao_Holkar "Male Rao Holkar") became the ruler of Indore in 1766, under Ahilya Bai's regency, but he too died within few months in April 1767. Ahilya Bai became the ruler of Indore after the death of her son with Khande Rao. [Ahilya Bai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ahilyabai_Holkar "Ahilyabai Holkar") was a great pioneer and builder of Hindu temples who constructed hundreds of temples and [Dharmashalas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dharamshala_(type_of_building) "Dharamshala (type of building)") throughout India.

In 1818, the [Holkars](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/House_of_Holkar "House of Holkar") were defeated by the [British](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_Empire "British Empire") during the [Third Anglo-Maratha War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Third_Anglo-Maratha_War "Third Anglo-Maratha War"), in the [Battle of Mahidpur](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battle_of_Mahidpur "Battle of Mahidpur") by which the capital was again moved from Maheshwar to Indore. A residency with British residents was established at Indore, but Holkars continued to rule [Indore State](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore_State "Indore State") as a [princely state](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Princely_state "Princely state") mainly due to efforts of their [Dewan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dewan "Dewan") Tatya Jog. During that time, Indore has established the headquarters of the British Central Agency. [Ujjain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ujjain "Ujjain") was originally the commercial centre of Malwa. But the British administrators such as [John Malcolm](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Malcolm "John Malcolm") decided to promote Indore as an alternative to Ujjain because the merchants of Ujjain had supported anti-British elements.[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-AF_1998-43)

In 1906 electric supply was started in the city, the fire brigade was established in 1909, and 1918, the first master-plan of the city was made by noted architect and town planner, [Patrick Geddes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Patrick_Geddes "Patrick Geddes").[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-Geddes-44) During the period of [Maharaja Tukoji Rao Holkar II](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tukojirao_Holkar_II "Tukojirao Holkar II") (1852–86) efforts were made for the planned development and industrial development of Indore. With the introduction of Railways in 1875, the business in Indore flourished during the reigns of [Maharaja Shivaji Rao Holkar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shivajirao_Holkar "Shivajirao Holkar"), [Maharaja Tukoji Rao Holkar III](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tukojirao_Holkar_III "Tukojirao Holkar III") and [Maharaja Yeshwant Rao Holkar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yeshwantrao_Holkar_II "Yeshwantrao Holkar II").

### Post-independence

After India's independence in 1947, Holkar State, along with several neighbouring princely states, acceded to the Indian Union. On 1 November 1956, when [Madhya Bharat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Madhya_Bharat "Madhya Bharat") was merged into [Madhya Pradesh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Madhya_Pradesh "Madhya Pradesh"), Indore became part of the newly formed state. Indore a city today of nearly 4.5 million (2018) residents, has been transformed from a traditional commercial urban centre into the modern dynamic commercial capital of the state. In December 2025, a [drinking water contamination](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_Indore_drinking_water_contamination "2025 Indore drinking water contamination") incident occurred in Bhagirathpura, a neighbourhood of Indore. The incident resulted in the deaths of 21 people, while approximately 1,400 residents experienced gastrointestinal symptoms consistent with a waterborne infection.[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-47)

## Geography

### Climate

Indore lies on a borderline between a [tropical savanna climate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropical_savanna_climate "Tropical savanna climate") (_Aw_) and a [humid subtropical climate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Humid_subtropical_climate "Humid subtropical climate") ([Köppen climate classification](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/K%C3%B6ppen_climate_classification "Köppen climate classification")_Cwa_). Because of its high elevation the climate is much more moderate compared to the _[North Indian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/North\_Indian "North Indian")_ plains, even during the hottest months the nights are relatively cool, which is known as _[Shab-e-Malwa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shab-e-Malwa "Shab-e-Malwa")_.[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-48) Three distinct seasons are observed: summer, monsoon and winter. The coldest temperature was 1.1°C (34.0°F) on 27 December 1936.[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-49)

Indore gets moderate rainfall of 700 to 800 mm (28 to 31 in) during June–September due to the [southwest monsoon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Monsoon "Monsoon").

### Water bodies

Indore is home to several significant water bodies, two of which have achieved international recognition as [Ramsar Sites](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ramsar_site "Ramsar site").[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-59) Currently, while the [Narmada River](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Narmada_River "Narmada River") project supplies a significant portion of the city's demand, the presence and conservation of local lakes is deemed essential for mitigating the nightmare of flash floods and ensuring long-term water security.[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-60)

## Demographics

See also: [List of cities in Madhya Pradesh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_cities_in_Madhya_Pradesh "List of cities in Madhya Pradesh")

Indore is the most populous city in Madhya Pradesh. It is also the largest [metropolitan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metropolis "Metropolis") city in Central India. According to the 2011 census of India, the population of Indore city (the area under the municipal corporation and outgrowths) was 1,994,397.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-CensusGov2011-7)[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-census_city-61) The population of the Indore metropolis ([urban agglomeration](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urban_agglomeration "Urban agglomeration") that includes neighbouring areas) was 2,170,295.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-census_metro-8) In 2011, the city had a population density of 25,170 people per square mile (9,718 per square km), rendering it the most densely populated of all the municipalities with population over 100,000 in [Madhya Pradesh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Madhya_Pradesh "Madhya Pradesh"). As per the 2011 census, 1,502,775 were literates, which translates to 75.4% of the total population, with an effective literacy rate (of population 7 years and above) 85.5%, with male literacy of 89.8% and female literacy was 81.2%.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-CensusGov2011-7) The [Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scheduled_Castes_and_Scheduled_Tribes "Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes") populations in 2011 were 309,229 and 54,075, respectively. The total number of households were 404711.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-CensusGov2011-7)

According to the 2011 census of India, the population of Indore city (the area under the municipal corporation and outgrowths) was 1,994,397.[[62]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-62) As per estimates, the population in 2025 is approximately 3,482,830.[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-63)

## Government and politics

### Civic administration

Main article: [Indore Municipal Corporation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore_Municipal_Corporation "Indore Municipal Corporation")

Indore has a city government, or municipality, with a mayor-council form of government. In 1870, the first municipality was constituted in Indore. Bakshi Khuman Singh (Commander In Chief) of Holkar State Army was appointed as chairman.[[71]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-:3-71) Indore municipality became the first city to have an elected municipal government responsible for the welfare and growth of the city.[[71]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-:3-71) In 1956, during the reorganisation of states, Indore was included in [Madhya Pradesh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Madhya_Pradesh "Madhya Pradesh"), and later that same year, was declared a [municipal corporation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Municipal_corporation "Municipal corporation").[[71]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-:3-71)

[Indore Municipal Corporation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore_Municipal_Corporation "Indore Municipal Corporation") (IMC) is spread over an area of 269 square km.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-villages-5)[[72]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-72) The Indore Municipal Corporation (IMC) is a unicameral body consisting of 69 Council members whose districts are divided into 12 zones and these zones had been further divided into 69 [wards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ward_(electoral_subdivision) "Ward (electoral subdivision)") defined by geographic population boundaries.[[73]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-73) In 2014, 29 villages were added into the fold of the municipality.[[74]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-74) In 2015, 23 more villages were added. After these inclusions, the number of wards went up to 85, and zones 19.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-villages-5)[[75]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-75)

The mayor and [councillors](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Councillor "Councillor") are elected to five-year terms. The municipal or local elections to Indore Municipal Corporation were last held in 2015.[[76]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-76)[[77]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-77) The next elections were to be held early in 2020, but as per a report from February 2020, these have not happened, although preparation of voter rolls and ward reservation happened later in July.[[78]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-78)[[79]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-79)[[80]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-80) The elected wing of the city government is headed by the Mayor and the incumbent Mayor is Pushya Mitra Bhargava. As per a report from the [Free Press Journal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Free_Press_Journal "The Free Press Journal"), Indore was notified in 2018 for not having constituted ward committees.[[81]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-81) The executive wing is headed by Pratibha Pal, the [municipal commissioner](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Municipal_Commissioner_(India) "Municipal Commissioner (India)") of Indore, who is also the first female commissioner of the city.[[82]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-82)

On 8 May 2020, the budget for of ₹ 4,763 crore for 2020–21 was approved for the civic body.[[83]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-83) Major sources of revenue for the municipality include collection of property tax, water tax, rent.[[84]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-84)[[85]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-85)

Indore municipality follows the guidelines as per the [Madhya Pradesh Municipal Corporations Act 1956](http://www.janaagraha.org/asics/report/Madhya-Pradesh-Municipal-Corporation-Act-1956.pdf)[Archived](https://web.archive.org/web/20180920174748/http://www.janaagraha.org/asics/report/Madhya-Pradesh-Municipal-Corporation-Act-1956.pdf) 20 September 2018 at the [Wayback Machine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wayback_Machine "Wayback Machine"), as well as the [Madhya Pradesh Municipalities Act, 1961](https://www.indiacode.nic.in/bitstream/123456789/3583/1/Municipal%20Corporation%20ACT%201961.pdf).[[86]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-86) The IMC is responsible for public education, correctional institutions, libraries, public safety, recreational facilities, sanitation, water supply, local planning, and welfare services.

### Municipal finance

### Law and order

The [Indore Police](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore_Police "Indore Police"), a division of the [Madhya Pradesh Police](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Madhya_Pradesh_Police "Madhya Pradesh Police"), is under the direct control of Department of Home Affairs. The [government of Madhya Pradesh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Government_of_Madhya_Pradesh "Government of Madhya Pradesh") is the law enforcement agency in Indore. Indore district is divided into 39 police stations and seven police outposts.[[98]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-98)

In 2012, it was reported that the Police Commissionerate system would be implemented in Indore, but this did not pan out because of tussle between the IAS and IPS officers in the state.[[99]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-99) The bill was proposed again in 2018 and has been criticised by NewsClick.[[100]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-100) The system has not been implemented as of 2020, although there has been talk of it.[[101]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-101)

As of 4 September 2013, the Divisional commissioner is Dr Pawan Kumar Sharma.[[102]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-102) In Feb 2020, the new [Director General of Police](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Director_general_of_police "Director general of police") became Vivek Johri while SSP Indore is Harinarayan Chari Mishra.[[103]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-103)[[104]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-104)

### Judiciary

Indore is also a seat for one of the two permanent benches of [Madhya Pradesh High Court](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Madhya_Pradesh_High_Court "Madhya Pradesh High Court") with [Gwalior](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gwalior "Gwalior"), the city, its agglomerates, and other 12 districts of western Madhya Pradesh falls under the jurisdiction of [Indore High Court](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore_High_Court "Indore High Court").

### Other agencies

Main article: [Indore Development Authority](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore_Development_Authority "Indore Development Authority")

Most of the regions surrounding the city are administered by the [Indore Development Authority](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore_Development_Authority "Indore Development Authority") (IDA). IDA works as an apex body for planning and co-ordination of development activities in the Indore Metropolitan Region (IMR) comprising Indore and its agglomeration covering an area of 398.72 km 2 (153.95 sq mi). Primarily, IDA develops new residential areas. During the early stage of development of such areas, the IDA is responsible for developing basic infrastructure. Once a sizeable number of plots are sold, the area is formally transferred to the IMC, which is then responsible for the maintenance of the infrastructure in the area.[[105]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-105)

The IDA consists of two appointed components; the [collector](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/District_collector "District collector") of the [district](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore_district "Indore district"), who has executive powers, and the IDA Board which includes a chairman appointed by [Government of Madhya Pradesh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Government_of_Madhya_Pradesh "Government of Madhya Pradesh"), [Municipal Commissioner](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Municipal_Commissioner_(India) "Municipal Commissioner (India)") of Indore and five members form Town and Country Planning Department, Forest Department, Public Health Engineering, Public Works Department and MP Electricity Board[[106]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-106) who scrutinise the collector's decisions and can accept or reject his budget proposals each year. The role of IDA is to implement the master plan for Indore prepared by the Town and Country Office, Bhopal.[[107]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-107) The headquarters of the IDA is at Race Course Road, Indore.[[108]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-108)

## Civic utilities

Electricity in Indore is supplied by the Madhya Pradesh Paschim Kshetra Vidyut Vitaran Company Limited, the state's agency.[[109]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-109)[[110]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-110)

Major source of water in Indore are [Narmada River](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Narmada_River "Narmada River") and [overhead tanks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Water_tank "Water tank").[[111]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-:4-111) In 2016, the central government sanctioned 70 crores under the [AMRUT](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atal_Mission_for_Rejuvenation_and_Urban_Transformation "Atal Mission for Rejuvenation and Urban Transformation") scheme to overhaul the water facilities.[[111]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-:4-111) Indore used to receive 350 MLD of water from Jalud pumping station on Narmada river; while in 2019 the quantity reduced by 100 MLD, as of 2020 it has regained its capacity.[[112]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-112)[[113]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-113) The municipality supplies around 450 MLD water through piped connections to parts of the town on alternate days, other parts of the city have shortage of water.[[114]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-114) The urban poor and unauthorised slum area face a massive shortage of water, and need to purchases private water in drums, or need to have to access private tubewells.[[115]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-115)[[116]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-116) A joint study done by [UN Habitat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Nations_Human_Settlements_Programme "United Nations Human Settlements Programme"), IMC and [WaterAid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/WaterAid "WaterAid") mapping poverty surveyed 176545 households (approximately 1/3rd of the households in the city), and found that 72% of the households did not have access to piped water supply.[[117]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-117)

As of 2012, Indore generated nearly 240 MLD of sewage.[[118]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-118) As per a report from August 2018, Indore achieved 100% treatment of the faecal matter generated in the city.[[119]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-:5-119) The city has three [sewage treatment](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sewage_treatment "Sewage treatment") plants (STPs), which includes a [sequencing batch reactor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sequencing_batch_reactor "Sequencing batch reactor") with a capacity of 245 MLD, the largest in the world, as well as a 78 MLD and 12 MLD [Upflow anaerobic sludge blanket digestion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Upflow_anaerobic_sludge_blanket_digestion "Upflow anaerobic sludge blanket digestion") at Kabitkhedi and a third with a capacity of 122 MLD.[[119]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-:5-119)

As of 2019, Indore generates over 1,115 [metric tons](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tonne "Tonne") (MT) of garbage a day, of which 650 MT is [wet waste](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Waste_sorting "Waste sorting") and 465 MT is [dry waste](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Waste_sorting "Waste sorting").[[119]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-:5-119) The municipality has 100% door to door collection and segregation.[[119]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-:5-119) The city has a Centralized Processing Unit situated at Devguradia, Nemawar Road over an area of 146 acres. Waste collected at the garbage transfer stations in city is weighed, compressed and moved to this site for final processing.[[119]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-:5-119) Indore set up a Plastic Collection Centre (PCC) to reuse and recycle the city's [plastic waste](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plastic_pollution "Plastic pollution") and installed a plastic cleansing machine known as a 'Phatka Machine'.[[119]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-:5-119)

## Economy

Main article: [Economy of Indore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Economy_of_Indore "Economy of Indore")

Indore is a commercial centre for goods and services. As per the official records released by the Directorate of Economics and Statistics (Madhya Pradesh), the GDP (nominal) of [Indore District](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore_district "Indore district") is estimated at Rs. 64,813 crores for the year 2020–21.[[120]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-auto3-120) While its per-capita nominal GDP was recorded at INR 1,51,101 in 2020–21. The city also hosts a biennial global investors' summit, which attracts investors from several countries. Major industrial areas surrounding the city include [Pithampur](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pithampur "Pithampur") (phases I, II and III alone host 1,500 large, medium and small industrial set-ups[[121]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-121)), Indore Special Economic Zone (around 3,000 acres/ 4.7 square miles/ 1,214 hectares[[122]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-122)), Industrial Area at [Dewas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dewas "Dewas") I, II & III (around 745 acres/ 1.15 square miles/ 300 hectares) is in the close proximity to Indore (around 35 km), on NH-3 section between Agra- Bombay Road. Sanwer industrial belt (1,000 acres/ 1.6 square miles/ 405 hectares[[123]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-mpindustry.org-123)), Laxmibainagar Industrial Area, Rau Industrial Area, Bhagirathpura Industrial Area, Kali Billod Industrial Area, Ranmal Billod Industrial Area, Shivajinagar Bhindikho Industrial Area, Hatod Industrial Area.[[123]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-mpindustry.org-123)

The city also has IT Parks, Crystal IT Park (550,000 square feet), Pardeshipura IT Park (100,000 square feet[[124]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-124)), Electronic Complex, and Individual Special Economic Zones (SEZs) such as TCS SEZ, Infosys SEZ, Impetus SEZ, Diamond Park, Gems and Jewelry Park, Food Park, Apparel Park, Namkeen Cluster and Pharma Cluster.

## Culture

### Food

Indore's culinary culture has a blend of Maharashtrian, Malwi, Rajasthani and Gujarati influence. The street food of the city is especially popular. Two of the most noteworthy street food places in Indore are [Chappan Dukan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chappan_Dukan "Chappan Dukan") and [Sarafa Bazaar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sarafa_Bazaar "Sarafa Bazaar").[[135]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-:2-135)

As part of the Smart City project, the Chappan Dukan area has been developed as a smart food street. The cost of this project is ₹ 40 million and has been implemented in a 45-day period.[[136]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-136)

Sarafa Bazaar, which is India's only night street-food market, attracts large crowds from the city and tourists from various places.[[137]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-:1-137)

Indore is also notable for its wide variety of _namkeen_ s or savoury items and has many popular _namkeen_ stores across the city. Most popular food items of Indore include poha, kachori, samosa, jalebi, gulab jamun, rabdi, gajak, imarti, bhel, pani puri, hot dog, egg banjo, moong bhajiya, moong daal halwa, dahi wada, [sabudana khichri](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sabudana_khichri "Sabudana khichri"), sabudana wada, _[dhokla](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dhokla "Dhokla")_, jeeravan, and sev.[[137]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-:1-137)

The city is debatably the most vegetarian city in India; nearly 49% of population is vegetarian at some level.[[138]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-138)

### Festivals

Rang Panchami is one of the most vibrant festivals celebrated in Indore, marked by a grand procession known as the "Ger".[[142]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-142) Unlike the Holi festival celebrated across India, Rang Panchami in Indore has a distinct cultural identity. Thousands gather in the old city area as traditional music, dancing, and colour-throwing fill the streets. Organised by local groups and supported by the municipal corporation, the event includes decorated trucks, DJs, and water cannons spraying coloured water. The celebration showcases Indore’s unique blend of tradition and modernity.

### Road

Indore is connected to other parts of India through National and State highways. The nearest cities to Indore by road are [Dewas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dewas "Dewas") (around 35 km), [Shajapur](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shajapur "Shajapur") (100 km), [Ujjain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ujjain "Ujjain") (around 57 km) and [Bhopal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bhopal "Bhopal") (around 200 km).

The National Highways passing through the city are:

*   [National Highway 52 (NH 52)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Highway_52_(India) "National Highway 52 (India)") contains parts of the erstwhile [NH3 (AB Rd stands for Agra Bombay Road)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Highway_3_(India,_old_numbering) "National Highway 3 (India, old numbering)") and it originates at [Sangrur, Punjab](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sangrur "Sangrur") and runs through [Jaipur, Rajasthan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jaipur,_Rajasthan "Jaipur, Rajasthan"), Indore, [Dhule](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dhule "Dhule") and terminates at [Ankola](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ankola "Ankola") in Karnataka.
*   [National Highway 47](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Highway_47_(India) "National Highway 47 (India)") starts from [Bamanbore, Gujarat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bamanbore "Bamanbore") and reaches Indore via [Ahmedabad](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ahmedabad "Ahmedabad") and further connects [Betul](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Betul,_Madhya_Pradesh "Betul, Madhya Pradesh") to terminate at [Nagpur](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nagpur "Nagpur").

The highways which have ceased to exist because of renumbering[[146]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-146) are:

*   [National Highway 3](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Highway_3_(India,_old_numbering) "National Highway 3 (India, old numbering)") also known as the Agra-Bombay Road or AB Road, is an important highway connecting [Agra](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Agra "Agra") to [Mumbai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mumbai "Mumbai") via Indore, Dewas, Gwalior &[Dhule](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dhule "Dhule").
*   [National Highway 59](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Highway_59_(India,_old_numbering) "National Highway 59 (India, old numbering)")& its branch NH 59A. NH 59 originated at [Ahmedabad](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ahmedabad "Ahmedabad") and passed through [Godhra](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Godhra "Godhra"), Indore, [Raipur](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Raipur "Raipur"), [Brahmapur, Odisha](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brahmapur,_Odisha "Brahmapur, Odisha") and terminated at [Gopalpur-on-Sea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gopalpur-on-Sea "Gopalpur-on-Sea") while NH 59A connected Indore &[Betul](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Betul,_Madhya_Pradesh "Betul, Madhya Pradesh").

The state highways passing through the city are:

*   [MP State Highway 27](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Madhya_Pradesh_State_Highway_27 "Madhya Pradesh State Highway 27") runs from [Jhalawar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jhalawar "Jhalawar") in Rajasthan, through [Ujjain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ujjain "Ujjain"), Indore, [Barwaha](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barwaha "Barwaha"), [Burhanpur](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burhanpur "Burhanpur") in Madhya Pradesh and terminates at [Malkapur, Buldhana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malkapur,_Buldhana "Malkapur, Buldhana") in Maharashtra.
*   MP State Highway 31 ([Neemuch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neemuch "Neemuch") – [Ratlam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ratlam "Ratlam") – [Dhar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dhar "Dhar"))
*   MP State Highway 18 connects Indore to [Dewas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dewas "Dewas"), [Bhopal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bhopal "Bhopal"), [Ujjain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ujjain "Ujjain") and [Ahmedabad](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ahmedabad "Ahmedabad").

### Public transport

Main article: [Indore City Bus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore_City_Bus "Indore City Bus")

Indore's City Bus transport system runs through 277 km (172 mi) of road with a daily ridership of over 140,000.[[147]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-147) Atal Indore City Transport Services Ltd, a PPP scheme operates buses and radio taxis in the city. The buses designated as City Bus operate on 64 Routes[[148]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-:0-148) with a fleet of 487 buses, with 421 bus stops.[[148]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-:0-148) The buses are colour-coded into three colours: Blue, Magenta and Orange according to their route.[[149]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-149)

Indore BRTS (iBUS) is a bus rapid transit system with 53 air-conditioned[[150]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-150) buses equipped with services like GPS and IVR which are used to track the position of the bus with information displayed on LED displays installed at the bus stops.

Indore Auto Rickshaw is a service for small distance travel. Daily approx. 500,000 people travel within the city.

[Indore Metro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore_Metro "Indore Metro") is a [rapid transit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rapid_transit "Rapid transit") system that has completed its successful first phase trail run.[[151]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-151)

Indore Cable Car was announced in January 2021 as another public transport for the city to decongest traffic. It will also be the first cable car in India to run on crowded streets.[[152]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-152)

Buses for other cities which are near Indore are operated by state transport and private transport operators. Cities like Ujjain, Dewas, Khandwa, Khargone are connected through daily road buses.

The [Daly College](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daly_College "Daly College"), founded in 1870 by General [Henry Daly](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Henry_Daly "Henry Daly"), is one of the oldest co-educational boarding school in the world, which was established to educate the rulers of the Central Indian princely states of the [Marathas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maratha_Empire "Maratha Empire") and [Rajputs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rajput "Rajput").[[153]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-lord-153)

The [Holkar Science College](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Holkar_Science_College "Holkar Science College"), officially known as Government Model Autonomous Holkar Science College was established in 1891.[[154]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-154)

Indore is the first city to have both IIT ([Indian Institute of Technology Indore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_Institute_of_Technology_Indore "Indian Institute of Technology Indore")) and IIM ([Indian Institute of Management Indore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_Institute_of_Management_Indore "Indian Institute of Management Indore")). Indore is home to a range of colleges and schools. Indore has a large student population and is a big educational centre in central India, it also is the education hub of central India.[[155]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-155) Most primary and secondary schools in Indore are affiliated with the [Central Board of Secondary Education (CBSE)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Central_Board_of_Secondary_Education "Central Board of Secondary Education"); however, quite a few numbers of schools are affiliated with ICSE board, NIOS board, CBSE board, and the state level M.P. Board as well.

[Indian Institute of Technology Indore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_Institute_of_Technology_Indore "Indian Institute of Technology Indore") is one of the most prestigious institutions in the country. Started in 2009, IIT Indore has its 500-acre campus in Simrol (28 km from Indore City). IIT Indore has several disciplines including Civil Engineering, Computer Science Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Metallurgy, and Material Science.

IIT Indore ranked 15 under the engineering category in the National Institute Ranking Framework. IIT Indore's central library emphasises the use of Online Information Resources. The library provides its users access to nearly 3800 electronic journals as well as access to databases such as ACM Digital Library, IEEE Xplore Digital Library, Science Direct, MathSciNet, JSTOR, SciFinder, Taylor and Francis, WILEY, and Springer. The library also provides air-conditioned and Wi-Fi enabled reading halls.

[Raja Ramanna Centre for Advanced Technology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Raja_Ramanna_Centre_for_Advanced_Technology "Raja Ramanna Centre for Advanced Technology") is a unit of [Department of Atomic Energy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Department_of_Atomic_Energy_(India) "Department of Atomic Energy (India)"), Government of India, engaged in [R&D](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/R&D "R&D") in non-[nuclear](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nuclear_engineering "Nuclear engineering") front-line research areas of [lasers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lasers "Lasers"), [particle accelerators](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Particle_accelerator "Particle accelerator") and related technologies. The centre is situated at the south-western end of the Indore, [Madhya Pradesh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Madhya_Pradesh "Madhya Pradesh").The RRCAT campus is spread over 760 hectares on the outskirts of Indore city. The campus encompasses laboratories, staff housing colony and other basic amenities like school, sports facilities, shopping complex, gardens etc.

[Devi Ahilya Vishwavidyalaya](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Devi_Ahilya_Vishwavidyalaya "Devi Ahilya Vishwavidyalaya"), also known as DAVV (formerly known as University of Indore or Indore Vishwavidyalaya), is a university in Indore with several colleges operating under its aegis. It has two campuses within the city, one at Takshila Parisar (near Bhavarkuan Square) and another at Rabindra Nath Tagore Road, Indore. The university runs several departments including [Institute of Management Studies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Institute_of_Management_Studies,_Devi_Ahilya_University "Institute of Management Studies, Devi Ahilya University"), School of Computer Science & Information Technology(SCSIT), (IMS), School of Law (SoL), [Institute of Engineering and Technology, DAVV](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Institute_of_Engineering_and_Technology,_DAVV "Institute of Engineering and Technology, DAVV") (IET), Educational Multimedia Research Centre (EMRC), International Institute of Professional Studies (IIPS), School of Pharmacy, School of Energy & Environmental Studies – one of the primer schools for MTech (Energy Management), School of Journalism and School of Futures Studies and Planning, which runs two MTech Courses with specialisations in Technology Management & Systems Science & Engineering, MBA (Business Forecasting), an MSc in Science & Technology Communication. The campus houses several other research and educational departments, hostels, playgrounds, and cafes.

**Indore** ([/ɪ n ˈ d ɔːr/](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:IPA/English "Help:IPA/English")[](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/transcoded/6/64/Indore.ogg/Indore.ogg.mp3 "Play audio")[ⓘ](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Indore.ogg "File:Indore.ogg"); [ISO](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_15919 "ISO 15919"): _Indaura_, Hindi:[[ɪn̪d̪ɔːr]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:IPA/Hindi_and_Urdu "Help:IPA/Hindi and Urdu")) is the largest city of the [Indian state](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_state_and_union_territory_capitals_in_India "List of state and union territory capitals in India") of [Madhya Pradesh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Madhya_Pradesh "Madhya Pradesh") where it serves as the [capital](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_state_and_union_territory_capitals_in_India "List of state and union territory capitals in India") and the administrative headquarters of the eponymous [district](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore_district "Indore district") and [division](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore_division "Indore division"). Modern-day Indore was established on the banks of the [Kanh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kanh_River "Kanh River") and [Saraswati](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saraswati_River_(Madhya_Pradesh) "Saraswati River (Madhya Pradesh)") rivers and traces its roots to its 16th-century founding as a trading hub between the [Deccan Plateau](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deccan_Plateau "Deccan Plateau") and [Delhi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Delhi "Delhi").[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-11)[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-12) Following the conquest of [Malwa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malwa "Malwa") by [Peshwa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peshwa "Peshwa")[Baji Rao I](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Baji_Rao_I "Baji Rao I"), the city came under the control of the [Maratha Empire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maratha_Confederacy "Maratha Confederacy") until its annexation by the [British East India Company](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_East_India_Company "British East India Company").[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-13)[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-14) Prior to [Indian independence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_independence_movement "Indian independence movement"), [the Kingdom of Indore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore_State "Indore State") was a nineteen [Gun Salute](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Salute_state "Salute state")[Princely State](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Princely_State "Princely State") of the [British Raj](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_Raj "British Raj") with the [Holkars](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/House_of_Holkar "House of Holkar") as rulers.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-15)

With an estimated population of 5.6 million in 2025 distributed over nearly 10 thousand square kilometres, the metropolitan region encompassing Indore, [Ujjain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ujjain "Ujjain"), [Dewas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dewas "Dewas"), [Pithampur](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pithampur "Pithampur") and [Nagda](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nagda "Nagda") serves as the financial capital of Madhya Pradesh. One of India's main industrial hubs, the metropolitan region is a major center for pharmaceutical and automotive manufacturing with, notably, [Asia’s longest test track](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NATRAX "NATRAX").[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-16)[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-17)[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-18)[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-19)[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-:6-20)

The largest education hub in central India, it is home to an [Indian Institute of Technology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_Institute_of_Technology_Indore "Indian Institute of Technology Indore") and an [Indian Institute of Management](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_Institute_of_Management_Indore "Indian Institute of Management Indore") and is one of the cities selected under the [central government's](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Government_of_India "Government of India") flagship [Smart Cities Mission](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smart_Cities_Mission "Smart Cities Mission") and [Swachh Survekshan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Swachh_Survekshan "Swachh Survekshan") programmes.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-21)[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-22)[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-23)[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-24)

Consistently ranked as India's [cleanest city](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_cleanest_cities_in_India "List of cleanest cities in India"), Indore is regularly commended for its clean air and proper waste management.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-25)[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-26)[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-27)[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-28)[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-29)[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-30)

## Etymology

[Gupta](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gupta_Empire "Gupta Empire") inscriptions name Indore as "Indrapura".[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-auto1-31) It is believed that the city is named after its Indreshwar Mahadev Temple, where [Shiva](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shiva "Shiva") is the presiding deity.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-32)[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-33) It is believed that [Indra](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indra "Indra") himself did _[Tapasya](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tapas\_(Indian\_religions) "Tapas (Indian religions)")_ (meditation) in this place and led sage Swami Indrapuri to establish the temple. Later, [Tukoji Rao Holkar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tukoji_Rao_Holkar "Tukoji Rao Holkar") who belonged to the Holkar clan of the Marathas and was the feudatory of Indore, renovated the temple.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-34) The older name of Indore is believed to be **Indur**, as referenced in historical records.[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-35) In 2017, a proposal was brought forward by the Indore Municipal Corporation to rename the city as "Indur".[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-36)[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-37)

## History

### Gupta Empire (Gupta era)

[Gupta Empire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gupta_Empire "Gupta Empire") inscription mentions Indore as city/town of Indrapura in Gupta Indore Copper plate inscription dated 146 Gupta era or 465 CE.[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-38) These are also some of the earliest mentions of Indore where the city is mentioned as 'Indrapura'.[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-39) Indrapura (modern day Indore) was then known for its sun temple, where in 464–65 CE, Gupta king [Skandagupta](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Skandagupta "Skandagupta") had made an endowment for the permanent maintenance of the city's sun temple. The temple was constructed by two merchants of the city – Achalavarman and Bhṛikuṇṭhasiṁha.[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-auto1-31)[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-40)

### Holkar era (Maratha Empire)

Main article: [Holkar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Holkar "Holkar")

During the [Mughal era](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mughal_Empire "Mughal Empire"), the area under the modern Indore district was equally divided between the administrations (_[sarkar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sarkar\_(administrative\_division) "Sarkar (administrative division)")_ s) of [Ujjain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ujjain "Ujjain") and [Mandu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mandu,_Madhya_Pradesh "Mandu, Madhya Pradesh"). Kampel was the headquarters of a _mahal_ (administrative unit) under the Ujjain _sarkar_ of [Malwa Subah](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malwa_Subah "Malwa Subah") (province). The area of the modern Indore city was included in the [Kampel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kampel,_Indore "Kampel, Indore")[pargana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pargana "Pargana") (administrative unit).[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-gazetteer_1971-41)

In 1715, the [Marathas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maratha_Empire "Maratha Empire") invaded this region (Mughal territory) and demanded [chauth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chauth "Chauth") (tax) from the Mughal _Amil_ (administrator) of Kampel. The Amil fled to [Ujjain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ujjain "Ujjain"), and the local [zamindars](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zamindar "Zamindar") agreed to pay Chauth to the Marathas. The chief zamindar, [Nandlal Chaudhary](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rao_Nandlal_Chaudhary "Rao Nandlal Chaudhary") (later known as Nandlal Mandloi), paid a chauth of around Rs. 25,000 to the Marathas. [Jai Singh II](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jai_Singh_II "Jai Singh II"), the Mughal Governor of Malwa, reached Kampel on 8 May 1715, and defeated the Marathas in a battle near the village. The Marathas came back in early 1716, and raided Kampel in 1717. In March 1718, the Marathas, led by [Santaji Bhonsale](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bhonsle_(clan) "Bhonsle (clan)"), invaded Malwa again, but were unsuccessful this time.

By 1720, the headquarters of the local pargana were transferred from Kampel to Indore, due to the increasing commercial activity in the city. In 1724, the Marathas under the new [Peshwa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peshwa "Peshwa")[Baji Rao I](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Baji_Rao_I "Baji Rao I"), launched a fresh attack on the Mughals in Malwa. Baji Rao I himself led the campaign, accompanied by his lieutenants [Udaji Rao Pawar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dhar_State "Dhar State"), [Malhar Rao Holkar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malhar_Rao_Holkar "Malhar Rao Holkar") and [Ranoji Scindia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ranoji_Scindia "Ranoji Scindia"). The Mughal [Nizam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Qamar-ud-din_Khan,_Asaf_Jah_I "Qamar-ud-din Khan, Asaf Jah I") met the [Peshwa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peshwa "Peshwa") at [Nalchha](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nalchha "Nalchha") on 18 May 1724, and acceded to his demand of collecting chauth from the area. The Peshwa returned to the [Deccan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deccan "Deccan"), but left [Malhar Rao Holkar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malhar_Rao_Holkar "Malhar Rao Holkar") at Indore to oversee the chauth collection.

The Marathas maintained friendly relations with Nandlal Chaudhary, who held influence over the local [Sardars](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sardar "Sardar") (chiefs). In 1728, they defeated the Mughals decisively in the battle of [Amjhera](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battles_involving_the_Maratha_Empire "Battles involving the Maratha Empire"), and consolidated their authority in the area over the next few years. On 3 October 1730, [Malhar Rao Holkar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malhar_Rao_Holkar "Malhar Rao Holkar") was appointed as the Maratha chief of [Malwa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malwa "Malwa"). The local zamindars, who had the title of [Chaudhari](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chowdhury "Chowdhury"), came to be known as _Mandloi_ s (after [mandal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tehsil "Tehsil"), an administrative unit) during the [Maratha reign](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maratha_Empire "Maratha Empire"). The [Holkar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/House_of_Holkar "House of Holkar") dynasty of the Marathas, which controlled the region, conferred the title of _Rao_ upon the local zamindar family.[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-42) After Nandlal died, his son Tejkarana was accepted as the _Mandloi_ of Kampel by the [Peshwa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peshwa "Peshwa")[Baji Rao I](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Baji_Rao_I "Baji Rao I"). The pargana was formally granted to [Malhar Rao Holkar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malhar_Rao_Holkar "Malhar Rao Holkar") by merging 28 and one-half Pargana by the Peshwa in 1733. The pargana headquarters were transferred back to Kampel during his reign. After his death, his daughter-in-law [Ahilyabai Holkar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ahilyabai_Holkar "Ahilyabai Holkar") moved the headquarters to Indore in 1766. The [tehsil](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tehsil "Tehsil") of Kampel was converted into Indore tehsil by a change in the name.[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-gazetteer_1971-41) Ahilyabai Holkar moved the state's capital to [Maheshwar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maheshwar "Maheshwar") in 1767, but Indore remained an important commercial and military centre.

### Princely State (Indore/Holkar State)

Main article: [Indore State](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore_State "Indore State")

See also: [Dewas Junior](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dewas_Junior "Dewas Junior"), [Dewas Senior](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dewas_Senior "Dewas Senior"), [Dhar State](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dhar_State "Dhar State"), and [Gwalior State](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gwalior_State "Gwalior State")

[![Image 22](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/25/Ahilya_Bai_Holkar_2025_stamp_of_India.jpg/250px-Ahilya_Bai_Holkar_2025_stamp_of_India.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Ahilya_Bai_Holkar_2025_stamp_of_India.jpg)

[Ahilyabai Holkar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ahilyabai_Holkar "Ahilyabai Holkar") on a 2025 stamp of India

[Ahalyabai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ahilyabai_Holkar "Ahilyabai Holkar") Holkar is fondly remembered as a noble, saintly and courageous woman. She ruled the kingdom of Indore (which was then part of the wider [Maratha Empire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maratha_Empire "Maratha Empire")) for several decades. Her rule is remembered as a golden age in Indore's history. From an agricultural background herself, she married Khande Rao, prince of Indore. Thereafter, she resided in the Royal Palace. Later, she was trained in statecraft and accompanied the army to war on many occasions. At that time the [Maratha Empire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maratha_Empire "Maratha Empire") (which was founded by [Chhatrapati Shivaji Raje Bhonsale](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shivaji "Shivaji")) was at the apex of its power. There were frequent battles and skirmishes, both against foreigners as well as internal feuds. In one such battle in 1754, [Ahalyabai's](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ahilyabai_Holkar "Ahilyabai Holkar") husband was killed. Her aged father-in-law ([Malhar Rao](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malhar_Rao_Holkar "Malhar Rao Holkar")) was shattered at the death of his son. He summoned Ahalyabai, who he loved deeply, and said: "You are now my son. I wish that you look after my kingdom".[Malhar Rao Holkar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malhar_Rao_Holkar "Malhar Rao Holkar") died in 1766, 12 years after the death of his son Khande Rao. Malhar Rao's grandson and Khande Rao's only son [Male Rao Holkar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Male_Rao_Holkar "Male Rao Holkar") became the ruler of Indore in 1766, under Ahilya Bai's regency, but he too died within few months in April 1767. Ahilya Bai became the ruler of Indore after the death of her son with Khande Rao. [Ahilya Bai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ahilyabai_Holkar "Ahilyabai Holkar") was a great pioneer and builder of Hindu temples who constructed hundreds of temples and [Dharmashalas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dharamshala_(type_of_building) "Dharamshala (type of building)") throughout India.

In 1818, the [Holkars](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/House_of_Holkar "House of Holkar") were defeated by the [British](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_Empire "British Empire") during the [Third Anglo-Maratha War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Third_Anglo-Maratha_War "Third Anglo-Maratha War"), in the [Battle of Mahidpur](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battle_of_Mahidpur "Battle of Mahidpur") by which the capital was again moved from Maheshwar to Indore. A residency with British residents was established at Indore, but Holkars continued to rule [Indore State](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore_State "Indore State") as a [princely state](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Princely_state "Princely state") mainly due to efforts of their [Dewan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dewan "Dewan") Tatya Jog. During that time, Indore has established the headquarters of the British Central Agency. [Ujjain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ujjain "Ujjain") was originally the commercial centre of Malwa. But the British administrators such as [John Malcolm](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Malcolm "John Malcolm") decided to promote Indore as an alternative to Ujjain because the merchants of Ujjain had supported anti-British elements.[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-AF_1998-43)

In 1906 electric supply was started in the city, the fire brigade was established in 1909, and 1918, the first master-plan of the city was made by noted architect and town planner, [Patrick Geddes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Patrick_Geddes "Patrick Geddes").[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-Geddes-44) During the period of [Maharaja Tukoji Rao Holkar II](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tukojirao_Holkar_II "Tukojirao Holkar II") (1852–86) efforts were made for the planned development and industrial development of Indore. With the introduction of Railways in 1875, the business in Indore flourished during the reigns of [Maharaja Shivaji Rao Holkar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shivajirao_Holkar "Shivajirao Holkar"), [Maharaja Tukoji Rao Holkar III](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tukojirao_Holkar_III "Tukojirao Holkar III") and [Maharaja Yeshwant Rao Holkar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yeshwantrao_Holkar_II "Yeshwantrao Holkar II").

### Post-independence

After India's independence in 1947, Holkar State, along with several neighbouring princely states, acceded to the Indian Union. On 1 November 1956, when [Madhya Bharat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Madhya_Bharat "Madhya Bharat") was merged into [Madhya Pradesh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Madhya_Pradesh "Madhya Pradesh"), Indore became part of the newly formed state. Indore a city today of nearly 4.5 million (2018) residents, has been transformed from a traditional commercial urban centre into the modern dynamic commercial capital of the state. In December 2025, a [drinking water contamination](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_Indore_drinking_water_contamination "2025 Indore drinking water contamination") incident occurred in Bhagirathpura, a neighbourhood of Indore. The incident resulted in the deaths of 21 people, while approximately 1,400 residents experienced gastrointestinal symptoms consistent with a waterborne infection.[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-47)

## Geography

### Climate

Indore lies on a borderline between a [tropical savanna climate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropical_savanna_climate "Tropical savanna climate") (_Aw_) and a [humid subtropical climate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Humid_subtropical_climate "Humid subtropical climate") ([Köppen climate classification](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/K%C3%B6ppen_climate_classification "Köppen climate classification")_Cwa_). Because of its high elevation the climate is much more moderate compared to the _[North Indian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/North\_Indian "North Indian")_ plains, even during the hottest months the nights are relatively cool, which is known as _[Shab-e-Malwa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shab-e-Malwa "Shab-e-Malwa")_.[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-48) Three distinct seasons are observed: summer, monsoon and winter. The coldest temperature was 1.1°C (34.0°F) on 27 December 1936.[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-49)

Indore gets moderate rainfall of 700 to 800 mm (28 to 31 in) during June–September due to the [southwest monsoon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Monsoon "Monsoon").

### Water bodies

Indore is home to several significant water bodies, two of which have achieved international recognition as [Ramsar Sites](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ramsar_site "Ramsar site").[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-59) Currently, while the [Narmada River](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Narmada_River "Narmada River") project supplies a significant portion of the city's demand, the presence and conservation of local lakes is deemed essential for mitigating the nightmare of flash floods and ensuring long-term water security.[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-60)

## Demographics

See also: [List of cities in Madhya Pradesh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_cities_in_Madhya_Pradesh "List of cities in Madhya Pradesh")

Indore is the most populous city in Madhya Pradesh. It is also the largest [metropolitan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metropolis "Metropolis") city in Central India. According to the 2011 census of India, the population of Indore city (the area under the municipal corporation and outgrowths) was 1,994,397.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-CensusGov2011-7)[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-census_city-61) The population of the Indore metropolis ([urban agglomeration](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urban_agglomeration "Urban agglomeration") that includes neighbouring areas) was 2,170,295.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-census_metro-8) In 2011, the city had a population density of 25,170 people per square mile (9,718 per square km), rendering it the most densely populated of all the municipalities with population over 100,000 in [Madhya Pradesh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Madhya_Pradesh "Madhya Pradesh"). As per the 2011 census, 1,502,775 were literates, which translates to 75.4% of the total population, with an effective literacy rate (of population 7 years and above) 85.5%, with male literacy of 89.8% and female literacy was 81.2%.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-CensusGov2011-7) The [Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scheduled_Castes_and_Scheduled_Tribes "Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes") populations in 2011 were 309,229 and 54,075, respectively. The total number of households were 404711.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-CensusGov2011-7)

According to the 2011 census of India, the population of Indore city (the area under the municipal corporation and outgrowths) was 1,994,397.[[62]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-62) As per estimates, the population in 2025 is approximately 3,482,830.[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-63)

## Government and politics

### Civic administration

Main article: [Indore Municipal Corporation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore_Municipal_Corporation "Indore Municipal Corporation")

Indore has a city government, or municipality, with a mayor-council form of government. In 1870, the first municipality was constituted in Indore. Bakshi Khuman Singh (Commander In Chief) of Holkar State Army was appointed as chairman.[[71]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-:3-71) Indore municipality became the first city to have an elected municipal government responsible for the welfare and growth of the city.[[71]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-:3-71) In 1956, during the reorganisation of states, Indore was included in [Madhya Pradesh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Madhya_Pradesh "Madhya Pradesh"), and later that same year, was declared a [municipal corporation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Municipal_corporation "Municipal corporation").[[71]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-:3-71)

[Indore Municipal Corporation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore_Municipal_Corporation "Indore Municipal Corporation") (IMC) is spread over an area of 269 square km.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-villages-5)[[72]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-72) The Indore Municipal Corporation (IMC) is a unicameral body consisting of 69 Council members whose districts are divided into 12 zones and these zones had been further divided into 69 [wards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ward_(electoral_subdivision) "Ward (electoral subdivision)") defined by geographic population boundaries.[[73]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-73) In 2014, 29 villages were added into the fold of the municipality.[[74]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-74) In 2015, 23 more villages were added. After these inclusions, the number of wards went up to 85, and zones 19.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-villages-5)[[75]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-75)

The mayor and [councillors](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Councillor "Councillor") are elected to five-year terms. The municipal or local elections to Indore Municipal Corporation were last held in 2015.[[76]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-76)[[77]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-77) The next elections were to be held early in 2020, but as per a report from February 2020, these have not happened, although preparation of voter rolls and ward reservation happened later in July.[[78]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-78)[[79]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-79)[[80]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-80) The elected wing of the city government is headed by the Mayor and the incumbent Mayor is Pushya Mitra Bhargava. As per a report from the [Free Press Journal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Free_Press_Journal "The Free Press Journal"), Indore was notified in 2018 for not having constituted ward committees.[[81]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-81) The executive wing is headed by Pratibha Pal, the [municipal commissioner](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Municipal_Commissioner_(India) "Municipal Commissioner (India)") of Indore, who is also the first female commissioner of the city.[[82]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-82)

On 8 May 2020, the budget for of ₹ 4,763 crore for 2020–21 was approved for the civic body.[[83]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-83) Major sources of revenue for the municipality include collection of property tax, water tax, rent.[[84]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-84)[[85]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-85)

Indore municipality follows the guidelines as per the [Madhya Pradesh Municipal Corporations Act 1956](http://www.janaagraha.org/asics/report/Madhya-Pradesh-Municipal-Corporation-Act-1956.pdf)[Archived](https://web.archive.org/web/20180920174748/http://www.janaagraha.org/asics/report/Madhya-Pradesh-Municipal-Corporation-Act-1956.pdf) 20 September 2018 at the [Wayback Machine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wayback_Machine "Wayback Machine"), as well as the [Madhya Pradesh Municipalities Act, 1961](https://www.indiacode.nic.in/bitstream/123456789/3583/1/Municipal%20Corporation%20ACT%201961.pdf).[[86]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-86) The IMC is responsible for public education, correctional institutions, libraries, public safety, recreational facilities, sanitation, water supply, local planning, and welfare services.
